topics.title: Concept of Place of Supply and Key Definitions
explain: GST is a destination-based tax levied where goods or services are consumed.
Place of Supply (POS) together with Location of Supplier (LOS) determines if a supply is intra-State (CGST+SGST) or inter-State (IGST).
For B2B supplies, tax paid is taken as input tax credit (ITC) by the recipient, so the Location of Recipient (LOR) is generally the POS.
For B2C supplies, tax revenue stays where consumption happens or where the supplier is located if address is unavailable.
Fixed establishment means a place with sufficient permanence and structure to supply or receive services.
Continuous journey means a travel booked on single/multiple tickets with no separate stopovers.

flow.title: Steps to Determine Nature of Supply
steps: Identify Location of Supplier (LOS)
Determine Place of Supply (POS)
Compare LOS and POS locations
If same State/UT: charge CGST and SGST
If different State/UT: charge IGST

topics.example: A registered firm in Noida buys consulting services from a Delhi CA. The GST credit passes through to Noida, making it an inter-State B2B transaction.
remember: Incorrect tax payment (e.g. paying CGST/SGST instead of IGST) requires paying correct tax and claiming a refund without interest penalty.
mistakes: Thinking 'location of supplier of goods' is defined in the IGST Act. Only 'location of supplier of services' is defined.

quiz.q: Why is determining the correct Place of Supply critical under GST?
o: It decides whether CGST/SGST or IGST applies to the transaction
It determines the income tax rate for the business
It allows the supplier to avoid paying any tax
It changes the customs duty rate on imported goods
quiz.why: Matching LOS and POS determines whether a supply is intra-State (CGST+SGST) or inter-State (IGST).

quiz.q: What happens if an inter-State transaction is wrongly treated as intra-State and tax is paid accordingly?
o: The supplier is sent to prison immediately
Correct tax must be paid and wrong tax refunded without interest penalty
The tax paid is forfeited with a 100% penalty
No correction is allowed after tax payment
quiz.why: GST law requires paying the correct tax and claiming a refund of the wrongly paid tax without interest.

topics.title: Place of Supply of Goods (Domestic Transactions)
explain: If supply involves movement of goods, POS is where movement terminates for delivery to recipient [Sec 10(1)(a)].
Under Bill-to-Ship-to model, goods delivered to third person on instructions of buyer deem buyer as recipient; POS is buyer's principal place of business [Sec 10(1)(b)].
If supply does not involve movement, POS is location of goods at the time of delivery [Sec 10(1)(c)].
For sales to unregistered persons, POS is delivery address recorded on invoice, else supplier location [Sec 10(1)(ca)].
If goods are assembled/installed at site, POS is the site of installation [Sec 10(1)(d)].
For goods supplied on board a conveyance, POS is where goods are taken on board [Sec 10(1)(e)].

flow.title: Determining POS for Goods
steps: Check if supply involves movement of goods
If movement exists: POS is destination point
If third-party directs delivery: POS is third-party location
If no movement: POS is delivery location
If assembled at site: POS is assembly site

topics.example: A Mumbai buyer orders a machine from Ranchi to be assembled in a refinery in Kutch, Gujarat. The POS is Kutch (assembly site).
remember: Bill-to-Ship-to has two supplies: Supplier to Third Person (POS = Third Person location) and Third Person to Recipient (POS = Delivery destination).
mistakes: Assuming POS for goods on board a train is where sold, rather than where goods were taken on board.

quiz.q: A company in Delhi buys a machine from Delhi for installation at its factory in Noida (UP). What is the Place of Supply?
quiz.why: Under Section 10(1)(d), for goods assembled or installed at site, POS is the location of installation.

quiz.q: Firm A (Gujarat) orders Firm B (Gujarat) to deliver goods directly to Firm C (Maharashtra). What is the POS for supply from B to A?
o: Gujarat (Principal place of business of A)
quiz.why: Under Section 10(1)(b) 'bill-to-ship-to', POS for first supply is the principal place of business of third party (A).

topics.title: Place of Supply of Services - General Default Rule
explain: Section 12 applies when both supplier and recipient of services are located in India.
General rule applies to all services not specifically covered under sub-sections 12(3) to 12(14).
For B2B supply (to a registered person), POS is the location of such registered recipient.
For B2C supply (to an unregistered person), POS is recipient's address on record, or supplier's location if address is not on record.

flow.title: General Rule Decision Path
steps: Check if service falls under specific sub-sections 12(3)-(14)
If not covered, check registration status of recipient
If recipient is registered (B2B): POS is LOR
If recipient unregistered (B2C) & address exists: POS is LOR
If recipient unregistered & no address: POS is LOS

topics.example: A Delhi CA provides tax advisory to an unregistered client from Delhi whose address is not recorded. POS is Delhi (location of supplier).
remember: B2B service default rule always uses Location of Recipient (LOR) as proxy.
mistakes: Applying performance location to general management consultancy services instead of LOR.

quiz.q: A Haryana CA provides business advisory service to a GST-registered company in Noida (UP). What is the POS?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(2)(a), B2B supply of general services has POS as the location of the registered recipient.

quiz.q: An unregistered person from Delhi buys over-the-counter advice at a bank in Gurugram without giving an address. What is the POS?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(2)(b)(ii), for B2C services where recipient address is not on record, POS is location of supplier.

topics.title: Services Related to Immovable Property & Lodging
explain: Services directly related to immovable property (architects, interior decorators, construction, estate agents) have POS as property location.
Lodging accommodation (hotels, inns, guest houses, houseboats) has POS as location of property/vessel.
Accommodation for functions (marriages, corporate events) on immovable property has POS as property location.
If property is located outside India, POS reverts to location of recipient (LOR).
If property spans multiple States, POS is divided among States based on contract terms, or nights stayed / land area / time spent.

flow.title: Immovable Property Service POS
steps: Identify property/vessel location
If property is located in India: POS is property location
If property is outside India: POS is location of recipient
If property spans multiple States: apportion value per rules

topics.example: A Mumbai architect designs a building to be constructed in Ahmedabad. POS is Ahmedabad (property location).
remember: Lodging stay across multiple hotels in different states without contract is apportioned by number of nights stayed in each property.
mistakes: Choosing property location outside India as POS. When property is abroad, POS becomes recipient location in India.

quiz.q: A Delhi resident stays at a hotel in Mumbai for a business trip. What is the Place of Supply of hotel accommodation?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(3)(b), POS for lodging accommodation is the location where the property is situated (Mumbai).

quiz.q: A Mumbai engineer provides design services for an Indian client's property located in Australia. What is the POS?
quiz.why: Proviso to Sec 12(3) states that if property is located outside India, POS is location of recipient.

topics.title: Performance-Based & Training Services
explain: Section 12(4) covers restaurant, catering, personal grooming, fitness, beauty treatment, and health/cosmetic services.
For Sec 12(4) services, POS is always the location where services are actually performed (no B2B/B2C distinction).
Section 12(5) covers training and performance appraisal services.
For Sec 12(5) training: if recipient is registered (B2B), POS is LOR; if unregistered (B2C), POS is actual performance location.

flow.title: Evaluating Performance & Training Services
steps: Check service category: Sec 12(4) vs Sec 12(5)
If Sec 12(4) (catering/grooming/health): POS is performance site
If Sec 12(5) training (B2B): POS is location of recipient
If Sec 12(5) training (B2C): POS is performance site

topics.example: A Kolkata makeup artist does makeup for an actress in Jaipur. POS is Jaipur (where service is actually performed).
remember: Sec 12(4) personal care services have NO B2B/B2C distinction—always performance location.
mistakes: Applying performance location to B2B corporate GST training. B2B training goes to LOR.

quiz.q: A Hyderabad businessman dines at a restaurant in Mumbai. What is the Place of Supply of the restaurant service?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(4), POS for restaurant/catering services is where the services are actually performed (Mumbai).

quiz.q: A Kolkata firm imparts training to employees of a GST-registered Guwahati company at its Mumbai office. Contract is with Guwahati office. POS is?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(5)(a), B2B training POS is the location of registered recipient (Guwahati).

topics.title: Admission to & Organisation of Events
explain: Section 12(6) covers admission to cultural, sporting, scientific, educational, entertainment events or amusement parks.
POS for admission services is where the event is actually held or park is located.
Section 12(7) covers organisation of events, conference, exhibition, sponsorship.
For Sec 12(7) event organisation: B2B POS is Location of Recipient (LOR); B2C POS is location where event is held.
If B2C event is held outside India, POS reverts to location of recipient.

flow.title: Event Service POS Rules
steps: Determine if service is Admission [12(6)] or Organisation [12(7)]
If Admission: POS is where event/park is located
If Organisation (B2B): POS is recipient location
If Organisation (B2C in India): POS is event site
If Organisation (B2C outside India): POS is recipient location

topics.example: A Delhi resident buys entry tickets for a circus in Gurugram. POS is Gurugram under Section 12(6).
remember: Admission tickets [12(6)] always depend on venue location regardless of recipient registration.
mistakes: Confusing admission tickets [12(6)] with event organisation services [12(7)].

quiz.q: A UP resident buys an entry ticket for an amusement park in Noida (UP). What is the POS?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(6), POS for admission to amusement park is where the park is located (Noida).

quiz.q: A Delhi event company organises an award event in Mauritius for a Gujarat registered merchant. What is the POS?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(7)(a), organisation of event for a registered person (B2B) has POS as recipient location (Gujarat).

topics.title: Transportation of Goods and Passengers
explain: Section 12(8) covers goods transportation (including mail/courier). B2B POS is LOR; B2C POS is location where goods are handed over.
Transporting goods outside India by Indian supplier to Indian recipient still follows Sec 12(8) rules.
Section 12(9) covers passenger transportation. B2B POS is LOR; B2C POS is embarkation point for continuous journey.
For B2C right to passage (future use, embarkation unknown, e.g. metro card/vouchers), POS is LOR address on record, else LOS.
Return journey is treated as a separate journey even if booked together.

flow.title: Transportation POS Decision
steps: Identify transport type: Goods [12(8)] or Passenger [12(9)]
Check recipient status: Registered (B2B) vs Unregistered (B2C)
Goods: B2B -> LOR; B2C -> Handover point
Passenger: B2B -> LOR; B2C -> Embarkation point

topics.example: An unregistered Delhi resident couriers goods from Kanpur to Bhopal. POS is Kanpur (handover location).
remember: Return journey tickets are treated as independent separate journeys for determining embarkation point.
mistakes: Assuming goods transported abroad by Indian firms to Indian clients are exempt from Sec 12(8) rules.

quiz.q: A registered firm in Chennai hires a transporter to move goods to Delhi. What is the POS?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(8)(a), goods transport service provided to a registered person has POS as recipient location (Chennai).

quiz.q: An unregistered passenger from Chennai buys a Delhi Metro smart card in Delhi without address record. What is POS?
quiz.why: Under Sec 12(9) proviso, when embarkation point is unknown for future passage and address is missing, POS is LOS (Delhi).

topics.title: Services on Board Conveyance & Telecommunications
explain: Section 12(10): Services on board a conveyance (flight, train, vessel) have POS as first scheduled point of departure.
Section 12(11): Telecommunication services are categorized into fixed lines, post-paid, pre-paid, and others.
Fixed line / DTH / leased circuit POS is installation location.
Post-paid mobile POS is billing address on record, else supplier location.
Pre-paid mobile via agent POS is agent address; directly sold POS is location of payment collection; online recharge POS is recipient address on record.

flow.title: Telecommunication & On-Board Services POS
steps: On-board service: POS is first scheduled departure point
Fixed line/Dish: POS is installation site
Post-paid mobile: POS is billing address on record
Pre-paid agent: POS is agent address
Pre-paid online recharge: POS is recipient address on record

topics.example: In-flight movie streamed on a flight departing Delhi for Mumbai has POS as Delhi (first departure point).
remember: Leased circuit spanning multiple states without contract is apportioned by number of circuit points in each state.
mistakes: Using passenger embarkation point for on-board services instead of first scheduled point of departure of conveyance.

quiz.q: A passenger streams an in-flight movie on a flight originating in Delhi bound for Mumbai. What is the POS?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(10), POS for on-board service is the first scheduled point of departure of conveyance (Delhi).

quiz.q: A Kolkata resident gets a landline installed at home by a telecom provider. What is the POS?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(11)(a), POS for fixed line telecom service is location of installation (Kolkata).

topics.title: Banking, Financial, Stock Broking, Insurance & Govt Ads
explain: Section 12(12): Banking & financial/stock broking POS is recipient location on record, else supplier location.
Section 12(13): Insurance services B2B POS is LOR; B2C POS is recipient location on records of insurer.
Section 12(14): Advertisement services to Government/statutory bodies POS is each State/UT where ad is disseminated.
Govt ad values are apportioned per Rule 3 (e.g. newspaper editions, billboard locations, train track length, TRAI subscribers).

flow.title: Financial, Insurance & Govt Ad POS
steps: Banking [12(12)]: Recipient address on record? -> Yes: LOR; No: LOS
Insurance [12(13)]: B2B -> LOR; B2C -> LOR on record
Govt Ads [12(14)]: POS in each State where disseminated
Apportion Govt ad values per Rule 3 specific metrics

topics.example: A non-account holder buys a demand draft at a bank branch in Pune. POS is Pune (supplier location) as address is not on record.
remember: Over-the-counter banking services to non-customers default to location of supplier.
mistakes: Treating vendor display hoardings for corporate clients as property lease [12(3)(a)] when vendor retains possession. It is general ad service [12(2)].

quiz.q: An unregistered person buys travel insurance at Mumbai airport giving his Gurugram address. What is the POS?
quiz.why: Under Section 12(13)(b), B2C insurance POS is the recipient location on records of supplier (Gurugram).

quiz.q: Government places print ad order across Delhi, UP, and Rajasthan newspaper editions. What is the POS?
o: Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan proportionately
No GST applies to Government ads
quiz.why: Under Section 12(14), advertisement services to Govt are treated as supplied in each respective State where disseminated.

topics.title: Inter-State, Intra-State & Territorial Waters Supplies
explain: Section 7: Inter-State supply occurs when LOS and POS are in 2 different States, 2 UTs, or a State and a UT.
Section 8: Intra-State supply occurs when LOS and POS are in the same State or same Union Territory.
Establishments of a person in different States or registered separately in same State are treated as distinct persons [Sec 8 Explanation 1].
Section 9: If LOS or POS is in territorial waters (up to 12 nautical miles), it is deemed located in the coastal State/UT nearest to baseline.

flow.title: Supply Classification & Territorial Waters
steps: Compare Location of Supplier (LOS) & Place of Supply (POS)
If LOS & POS in same State/UT -> Intra-State (CGST+SGST)
If LOS & POS in different States/UTs -> Inter-State (IGST)
If location is in Territorial Waters -> Deemed nearest baseline coastal State

topics.example: Fuel supplied to a vessel 5 nautical miles off Maharashtra baseline and 7 off Gujarat baseline has POS as Maharashtra.
remember: Territorial waters limit is 12 nautical miles from baseline under Maritime Zones Act 1976.
mistakes: Assuming SEZ supplies in same state are intra-State. SEZ supplies are always inter-State.

quiz.q: Supplier is in Punjab and POS is in Haryana. What type of supply is this?
quiz.why: Under Section 7(1), when LOS and POS are in two different States, it is an inter-State supply.

quiz.q: A supplier in Mumbai supplies bunker fuel to a vessel 5 nautical miles off Maharashtra coast and 8 nautical miles off Gujarat. POS is?
quiz.why: Under Section 9, supply in territorial waters is deemed located in coastal State with nearest baseline (Maharashtra at 5 NM).
